Question: A gumball machine contains \(9\) red, \(7\) white, and \(8\) blue gumballs. The least number of gumballs a person must buy to be sure of getting four gumballs of the same color is
Solution:
To avoid getting four gumballs of one color, a person can receive at most three of each color. With three colors, that allows at most
\[
3\times3=9
\]
gumballs.

Nine purchases really can fail to give four of a color: they could produce three red, three white, and three blue gumballs. The machine has enough of every color for this to happen.

A tenth gumball must belong to one of the three colors, pushing that color's count to at least four. Therefore the least number required is \(\boxed{10}\), choice \(\text{C}\).
